thesisQuality.note: Realized AI-connectivity growth plus current 1.6T roadmap support a strong durable thesis; customer concentration prevents a higher score.

financialOperatingMomentum.note: Fiscal-2026 revenue more than tripled year over year and latest-quarter profitability remained strong.

marketValuationOpportunity.note: 59.42x trailing P/E and 19.88x sales are demanding; 23.05x forward P/E and exceptional growth provide partial offset.

catalystScore.note: 1.6T optical expansion and DustPhotonics integration are material catalysts, but qualification/volume remain unproven.

governancePower.note: SEC transparency and executed capital actions are visible, but ATM/SBC and limited governance-specific evidence warrant conservative treatment.

alignment2036.note: High-speed, power-efficient connectivity is directly aligned with scaling AI fabrics through the 2036 horizon.

crossDivisionLeverage.note: Electrical and optical connectivity span multiple data-center link architectures, but current revenue remains concentrated in a narrow hyperscale customer set.

bottleneckControl.note: SerDes/DSP, AEC and SiPho integration address bandwidth/power/reach constraints; Credo participates directly in the constrained interconnect layer.

scenarioRobustness.note: Electrical plus optical portfolio provides architecture optionality, while CPO/vendor integration can still shift economics away from merchant content.

substitutionResilience.note: Portfolio breadth improves resilience, but linear optics, competing merchant stacks and vertically integrated vendors remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.note: Filings support operating continuity but do not establish unusually strong supplier/geographic resilience; conservative midrange score preserves this evidence limitation.

pricingPower.note: Strong profitability and differentiated products support some capture, but 71% top-two customer concentration limits demonstrated bargaining power.

customerConcentration.note: Top two customers represented 71% of quarterly revenue.

valuation.note: Premium trailing P/E and P/S create compression sensitivity.

dilutionCapitalAllocation.note: ATM issuance and material SBC are explicit owner dilution risks.

technologyExecution.note: Optical qualification, integration and architecture substitution remain execution risks.

aggregate.note: Aggregate risk conservatively balances severe concentration/valuation risks against strong liquidity and realized operating momentum.

primaryCoverage.note: Core financial, liquidity, concentration and dilution facts use current SEC filings.

freshness.note: Financial filing is September 2 and market context is September 17, 2026.

sourceIndependence.note: SEC and independent market-data lineage are distinct; issuer launch material is not treated as independent corroboration.

completeness.note: All required components are supportable, but governance, supply-chain and durable pricing-power evidence remain less granular and are scored conservatively.

scoreRecord.thesis: Credo is a high-growth AI interconnect supplier positioned across electrical and optical successor architectures, with strong realized execution but material customer concentration and valuation risk.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Top-two customer concentration, premium valuation and architecture/vendor substitution can sharply reduce economics despite strong current growth.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Evidence of 1.6T optical qualification/volume and sustained diversification while converting inventory/backlog into cash-generative revenue.

edges.from: accelerator density and east-west AI traffic
edges.mechanism: more accelerators and larger fabrics raise aggregate bandwidth while power and uptime constrain link choices
edges.falsifier: fabric architectures materially reduce interconnect bandwidth/content per accelerator or AI cluster scaling stalls

edges.from: copper reach/power limits at rising lane rates
edges.mechanism: shorter electrical reach and thermal budgets increase optical substitution pressure
edges.falsifier: electrical interconnect retains materially better reach/power economics than expected at future lane rates

edges.mechanism: in-house PIC plus DSP/diagnostics lets Credo participate when links migrate from AEC to optics
edges.falsifier: DustPhotonics integration fails qualification/volume or customers choose competing/in-house optical stacks

edges.mechanism: qualification loss, capex digestion or buyer bargaining at one hyperscaler can disproportionately affect results
edges.falsifier: sustained diversification reduces top-two share while maintaining growth and cash conversion

edges.mechanism: management builds inventory for unfulfilled backlog and product ramps
edges.falsifier: inventory/receivables persistently outgrow realized sales or require write-downs

edges.to: demand for 800G/1.6T electrical and optical interconnect
edges.mechanism: higher accelerator density raises link bandwidth, power-efficiency and uptime requirements
edges.falsifier: hyperscaler architectures materially reduce high-speed interconnect content per accelerator or competing architectures remove Credo's attach opportunity

edges.to: Credo optical addressable market and product integration
edges.mechanism: in-house SiPho PIC capability combines with DSP/SerDes and diagnostics
edges.falsifier: integration fails to translate into competitive products, qualification, or volume deployments

edges.mechanism: large customers deploy high-speed connectivity in scale-out/scale-up networks
edges.falsifier: customer capex digestion, architecture substitution, or qualification losses break the conversion from AI buildout to Credo shipments

edges.mechanism: a small number of buyers control a majority of revenue and receivables
edges.falsifier: sustained diversification materially lowers top-customer revenue share without sacrificing growth
